title: 밝은 종이색 디자인과 보상
problem: 흰 그림이 어두운 게임판에서 뜬금없는 흰 구멍처럼 보였다.
change: 밝은 종이색·마룬 글자·구분되는 숫자색으로 교체하고 당시 타임어택 점수 보상을 추가했다.
outcome: 전체 UI가 밝아졌다. 당시 보상은 이후 레벨 모드에서 제거됐으므로 현재 규칙으로 혼동하지 않는다.
method: Historical git archive in isolated temp directory; current Vite runtime; fresh storage; seeded Math.random and controlled clock; finite animations finished. No historical source changes. Not a historical phone photograph or participant experiment.

after.commitMessage:
Move to a paper skin, and pay time attack back for a good run (#14)

Three things.

The cover becomes cover2 — 4837x9540 in, a 1080x2130 WebP out at 253KB. Its
0.507 aspect is closer to a phone's than the old 0.447, so the `contain`
margins shrink with it. The old source is deleted.

The skin goes light, and the cover only confirmed the decision rather than
driving it. Clearing a block uncovers the picture hidden beneath, and those
pictures are toy renders on white — on a night-blue board every cleared square
opened as a glaring white hole, all the way to the end of the stage, which
undercuts the whole point of the mode. On paper the reveal is continuous.
Cream ground, maroon ink, the wordmark's orange and yellow for anything active.

The nine block colours are spaced around the wheel rather than chosen to
taste: the board is read in groups, so two confusable digits at 35px means the
eye beats the rules. 8 started as cyan, which put three blues on one board
next to 1 and 2, and is now chocolate — the one warm dark the paper carries.
The 81 hardcoded rgba values scattered through the screen files collapse into
--panel, --slab, --recess, --sheen and --scrim, so the next skin change is one
file rather than nine.

Time attack now pays for a good run, where before it only ran you out of tiles
faster. Every hundred points adds nine low tiles — nine is exactly one row on
a nine-wide board, and 1s, 2s and 3s are what long combinations are always
starved of, so it is fuel and not clutter. Five hundred buys thirty seconds
and a fresh board, once: a second extension would turn a good run endless,
which is the other mode. Both thresholds are read off the score rather than
remembered, which works because the mode has no take-backs, so nothing new is
stored. The HUD says what landed — a row appearing at the bottom of the board
is not something a player racing a clock notices on their own.

104 unit tests, layout, drag and feedback all green.
